subject: TEST
subtopic: Rational-number set inclusion and boundary examples
axis_note: ladder_position orders this TEST matrix only; it is not a learner estimate.

must_contain: Recognize a simple fraction such as 1/2 as rational.
Distinguish rational membership from integer/whole/natural membership.

controlled_variation.notice: non-integer rationals expose why narrower sets cannot contain every rational number

must_contain: Translate the word every into a universal set-membership claim.
Use one rational counterexample to reject a narrower candidate set.

controlled_variation.hold: the source set is all rational numbers
controlled_variation.notice: one counterexample defeats a universal membership claim

must_contain: State that Q is contained in R.
Explain why natural, whole and integer are not universal supersets of Q.

controlled_variation.vary: the wording of the classification prompt
controlled_variation.hold: the inclusion Q ⊂ R and a non-integer rational boundary example
controlled_variation.notice: the same inclusion logic transfers across equivalent verbal formulations

family.invariant_demand: Decide which number set must contain every rational number by combining a universal set-inclusion claim with a boundary rational example.
family.difficult_move: Reject familiar but too-narrow number sets using a counterexample instead of choosing them from habit.
family.independent_check: Test the claim with 1/2 or 3/4 and verify that the surviving target set still contains that rational number.

support_ladder.handed_over: A non-integer rational example and the instruction to test each candidate set are supplied.
A non-integer rational example is supplied; the learner chooses how to use it.
Only the universal classification prompt is supplied.
